neighbours.label: reaching a new level or record: fires where 'new/next level', 'new record', 'highest' is about to come (take X ⟦to⟧ the next level, set ⟦a⟧ new record, ⟦reached⟧ their highest); the output promotes ' new'
fire: The new coach promised to take the club to the next level this season.
Her latest album takes electronic pop to a whole new level.
The sprinter set a new national record in the 200 metres.
Gold prices climbed on Monday and reached a new all-time high.
Exports reached their highest level in thirty years.
This camera raises the bar and sets a new standard for low-light photography.
The software upgrade brings battery life to new heights.
With this win the team has set a new benchmark for the league.
quiet: The new coach promised to take the players to the beach after training.
Her latest album was recorded in a small studio.
The sprinter finished the 200 metres in fourth place.
Gold prices fell on Monday and returned to last week's range.
Exports stayed roughly flat compared with the previous year.
This camera comes with a strap and a spare battery.
The software upgrade fixes several bugs in the menu.
With this loss the team has dropped to the bottom of the league.

notes: Card: ' to' before 'the next level', 'set a' before 'new record', 'reach' before 'their maximum'. Probes: next level 0.71, reached their highest 0.59, new record high 0.55; 'to a wider audience' and 'bus to the hotel' ~0, 'set the table' 0.14.
